summary: Hormonal acne with irregular periods, mother's diabetes, three medicines including topicals with an application site, investigations, and a procedure planned for the next visit. Traps: spironolactone is first said as hundred milligram then corrected to fifty, and only fifty is ground truth; the clindamycin gel she bought herself is stopped and belongs in medicationHistory, not prescriptionItems; turmeric and multani mitti packs are stopped home remedies, not prescriptions; the patient's own sugar is normal, only the mother is diabetic.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hello, come in. Ananya, is it? And this is mummy?

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Yes doctor, I am her mother. We came from Kondapur.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, sit down both of you. Ananya, tell me, what is troubling you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Doctor, I have pimples for almost two years now. Mostly on the jawline and chin, and some on the cheeks. They are painful, big ones, and they leave dark marks.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Do they come more at any particular time of the month?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, actually, one week before periods they become much worse.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. That is an important point. How old are you now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Twenty four.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And what treatment have you tried so far?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I was using clindamycin gel, I bought it from the pharmacy myself after seeing on YouTube. And one salicylic face wash. Gel was okay in the beginning, now it is not working at all.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How long did you use the clindamycin?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Almost eight months, daily.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That is too long for an antibiotic gel alone, the bacteria become resistant. So we will stop the clindamycin gel. Don't use it anymore.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Stop it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Now tell me about your periods. Are they regular?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not really doctor. They are irregular. Sometimes they come after forty days, sometimes forty five, once it came after almost two months.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And how many days does the bleeding last? Heavy or normal?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Five days, normal flow. Pain on the first day, I take one Meftal Spas sometimes.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: When was your last period?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It started on the third of this month.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Any extra hair growth? On the chin, upper lip, or on the tummy?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little on the chin, I do threading every two weeks.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any hair fall from the scalp?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Normal I think. Some fall when I comb.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How is your sleep? What do you do for work?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I am in an IT company in Gachibowli, doctor. Night shifts twice a week for the US client. Sleep is not fixed, sometimes I sleep at three in the morning.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hmm. Irregular sleep also disturbs hormones. Try to keep at least seven hours, even on shift days. Any stress?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Work stress is there. And honestly the pimples themselves give stress. I don't feel like going for office meetings on video.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I understand. That is why we will treat it properly, not just with creams. It will take time but it will improve.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, I have sugar. Is that why she has all this? Hormones?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, so mother has diabetes, I will note that. It can run with this hormonal pattern, so it is good you told me. Ananya, any health problem for you, thyroid, sugar, anything?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No doctor. Last year in office health check up everything was normal, sugar also normal.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good. Let me check your weight and height. Weight fifty two kilos. Height one fifty eight centimetres. Okay, BMI is normal.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I go to the gym also, three days a week.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Very good. Any whey protein or supplements?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I was taking whey protein, I stopped one month back because my friend said it causes pimples.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Your friend is partly right. Whey can flare acne in some people. Better to get protein from dal, paneer, eggs. Now let me examine. Come under the light. Hmm. There are multiple red papules and a few pustules on the jawline and chin, some deep painful nodules on the lower cheeks, and post acne pigmentation on both cheeks. No scars, luckily. Skin type is four.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is it very bad, doctor?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I would call this moderate acne. Not severe, but not mild either. And the pattern, jawline, chin, worse before periods, irregular cycles, a little chin hair, it all points to a hormonal component. Possibly PCOS. We will confirm with tests.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: PCOS? Her cousin also has that. Doctor, she is getting married next year. Will this affect anything?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Many girls have PCOS and have no problem with marriage or children. We just need to know, so we treat it properly. Diagnosis for now, acne vulgaris with a hormonal pattern, probable PCOS.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I want these blood tests. Serum testosterone, prolactin, and TSH. And an ultrasound of the pelvis. Do the blood tests between day two and day five of your next period.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Day two to five. Okay. Testosterone, prolactin, TSH and ultrasound.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, sorry, prolactin or protein? I wrote protein.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Prolactin, amma. P R O L A C T I N. It is a hormone. Not protein.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Achha, prolactin. Sorry, sorry.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Correct. Now the medicines. Listen carefully, mummy also please listen.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Yes, yes, I am writing.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: First, tablet spironolactone. This works on the hormonal side, it reduces the oil and the pimples on the jaw. Spironolactone hundred milligram once daily after breakfast. Actually, wait. She is only fifty two kilos and this is the first time. Make that fifty, not hundred. Spironolactone fifty milligram, once daily after breakfast, for three months.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Spiro lactone fifty. Sorry, what is the name again?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Spironolactone. S P I R O. The pharmacy will know. Fifty milligram, one tablet after breakfast, three months.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Any side effects for this, doctor?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Some girls feel slight breast tenderness or the periods may come a little early or late in the first month. Drink enough water. And one important thing, you should not become pregnant while taking it. Since marriage is next year, that is fine, we will stop it before that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay doctor.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Second, adapalene gel, point one percent. Apply a pea size amount on the face, the full face including the jawline and chin, not only on the pimples. Once daily at bedtime, on dry skin, twenty minutes after washing. For three months.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: On the whole face or only on the pimples?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Whole face, thin layer. Avoid the corners of the eyes, nose and lips. In the first two weeks it can sting and peel a little. If it burns too much, apply every alternate night for one week and then daily.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Night, whole face.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Third, the sunscreen. Because adapalene makes the skin sensitive and you already have dark marks. Photostable Acne gel, it is a sunscreen for oily skin. Apply on the face once daily in the morning before you go out.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Doctor, that one is costly no? My friend uses it, she said nine hundred rupees.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Around that, yes. But one tube lasts nearly two months if you use the right amount. The dark marks will not fade without sun protection. The face wash you have at home is fine, no need to buy a new one.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, food? She eats lot of chocolates and sweets. Milk also she drinks two glasses a day.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Reduce sugar and sweets, definitely. Milk, try reducing to one glass and see. Curd is fine. Don't stop eating, just less junk. Exercise is good, continue the gym.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: At home we were applying turmeric and multani mitti packs. Neighbour aunty said it will dry the pimples.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Please stop those packs for now. Turmeric can stain and irritate, and with adapalene the skin will already be dry. Keep it simple. Only the things I am giving, nothing else on the face.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Can I wear makeup for office? Foundation, compact?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Light makeup is okay, choose products that say non comedogenic, and remove everything before sleeping. Never sleep with makeup on. And wash the makeup brushes once a week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay doctor, I'll do that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And these dark marks? Will they go?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: The marks will lighten slowly once the active pimples stop. To speed it up, at the next visit we will plan a chemical peel, a salicylic acid peel. Not today, the skin is too inflamed now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: How much does the peel cost?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Reception will tell you the exact package, it is usually a series of four sessions, every two to three weeks. We decide next time.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Doctor, can she do facial at the parlour before the engagement? It is in March.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: No parlour facials, no bleach, no scrubs for now. They will irritate the skin with adapalene. Before the engagement, we will plan something here, safely.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. And threading? I can continue?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Threading you can continue. If the chin hair increases, later we can discuss laser. Not now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay doctor.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So once more. Stop the clindamycin gel. Spironolactone fifty milligram once after breakfast for three months. Adapalene gel at bedtime on the full face for three months. Photostable Acne sunscreen every morning on the face. Blood tests on day two to five of the period, plus the ultrasound. And come back after six weeks with all the reports, then we plan the peel.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Six weeks. Thank you so much doctor.

turns.speaker: attendant
turns.text: Thank you doctor. Dhanyavaad.
